story_text.value:
Author here.

I have been reading papers and taking notes for years, using Zotero for the PDFs, Obsidian for the notes, and, recently, an AI chat tab for my questions. Gamma PDF is my attempt to make that one place.

In Gamma, you open a paper by simply pasting an arXiv (or DOI) link. Highlight a sentence, or drag a box round a figure, and it becomes a note beside the page with the quote and a link back.

You can ask the AI about a figure or some text, and you get an answer that cites a page you can click.

You can read and annotate papers on an iPad with the Apple Pencil. Notability (Goodnotes) import/export is supported.

You can connect to Zotero's cloud and use Gamma as a better Zotero client, or import your whole library with no effort.

You can deploy Gamma with Docker and read papers from anywhere.

You can connect Gamma to Codex (Claude) with Gamma MCP, using it as a knowledge base.

Try it without installing: https://gammapdf.com

title.value: Show HN: Gamma PDF – AI-native PDF reader, self-hosted

story_text.value:
I've resuscitated a project I was working on years ago.

I was tired of having nested `flat_map` making my code basically unreadable just to fetch a simple value. The idea is to make simple & readable the traversing of deeply nested structures like JSON responses, while staying in Ruby & keeping its flexibility. Here it goes:

    graphql_response.then(&'[data][repository][issues][edges]*([node][title])')
    # => ["Support negative indexes", "Document aggregates"]

    github_prs_response.then(&'*[draft].any?')
    # => true
It's different from jq or JSONPath in that: - it's a Ruby block so you can use it with `map`, `find`, etc. - you can call Ruby method from it - it doesn't automatically flatten arrays, you decide - it raises on `nil` by default (unless you use `&`, i.e. `[customer][address]&[city]`)

Obviously, it has drawbacks: - it's yet another syntax to learn - it monkey-patches `String` which might be a blocker for some

I'm really looking for feedback here, what do you think? Is it worth releasing a gem with this value proposition?

title.value: Show HN: String#to_proc` to Help Traversing JSON

story_text.value:
I am the founder of Human Assisted Intelligence and I believe AI can be used to reduce polarization and improve the way people communicate and reach agreement.

At https://mediationbench.com/, there are many frontier LLMs tested, but it is difficult to keep up. I've been trying to get more free openrouter or huggingface credits. Azure for OpenAI and Anthropic have both provided token credits. (Thank You!)

The research paper is there as well.

There have been efforts to use LLMs to lie and play diplomacy, which are excellent compliments to this work.

In v4, the test will get harder as Claude nearly saturated the test. Astra was surprisingly low, perhaps because of alignment or safety efforts.

I'd love to get feedback and hear from all of you. I've been working on related ideas for 20 years, so it's definitely a passion project with too much time in isolation.

title.value: Show HN: Feedback/AMA MeditionBench; LLMs for mediation and conflict resolution

story_text.value:
I missed a return window last month because the policy page and the order confirmation said different things.
Turns out return windows don't exist as data anywhere. So I've been reading them by hand. 248 shops, 8 countries. Each record stores the sentence the number came from, the URL and the date I read it. 331 more are in the list unread and marked as such.
Free, no signup. MCP server at pricemend.com/mcp if you want an agent to use it.
An early version of my parser read "within one year of the event date" off Target's gift registry page and recorded a 365 day return window. That's why there's a quote on every record now.
Is the confidence field useful, or over-engineered?

title.value: Show HN: I hand-read 248 shops' return policies because no dataset existed

story_text.value:
If you already have multiple coding agents(one kind of agent also works though), you should really look into this project! It's a desktop app that brings coding agents working together, with user experience similar to ChatGPT!

One kind of agent is enough for an agent team: all of one kind, or any mix of Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor Agent, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, Muse Code and five open-source coding agents on your own model backends. For each question, the lead agent designs the team: each member’s role and model, and how they take turns. Once you confirm it, the real agents on your machine work on your code, or any question, and answer each other.

It also supports voice input, notification, branching in conversation, task scheduling, and mobile app(PWA) support!

If you are interested in this project, please give it a try and star us on the GitHub repo, thanks!

GitHub repo: https://github.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay

title.value: Show HN: Harness Relay – the coding agents you have, working together
